gaps: pool_timeout_rate, pool_idle and connection-holder/leak metrics were not obtained because the corresponding calls exhausted the budget (ev_13, ev_14).
A longer pre-incident baseline for pool_used/pool_wait_p95 (beyond the short pool_pending baseline check) was not queried; budget cut the remaining metric calls (ev_15).
Additional Loki pattern mining, including grouping error lines by route or downstream host to identify what held the connections, was cut off by the budget (ev_16).
Host-level CPU, memory and container throttling metrics were not checked.
Log volume after the end of the queried window was not examined to confirm recovery time and whether the pool drained.
The exact timestamp of the first pool_used increase between the 14:29:11 and 14:29:26 samples was not resolved at finer granularity.
report.summary: Connection-pool saturation on demo-service caused the incident: the pool filled to its hard cap, requests queued for connections and then timed out, producing a simultaneous spike in HTTP p95 latency and 5xx error ratio. Database operation latency, event-loop delay and request rate stayed flat, so slow queries, CPU/event-loop saturation and a traffic surge are not consistent with the evidence. The trigger that made connections stay held in the pool (leak versus slow holder) remains unconfirmed.

timeline.event: Pool used connections first becomes non-zero (4) after a baseline of {used_base}; pool pending still {pend_base}.
First sampled Loki error line: 'request failed' — 'timeout exceeded when trying to connect'.
Pool reaches its cap of {pool_max} used connections with {pend_max} pending requests; HTTP p95 jumps to {lat_mid} s and 5xx ratio to {err_mid}.
Peak impact: HTTP p95 {lat_at_max} s, 5xx ratio {err_max}, pool wait p95 {wait_max} s, {pend_max} requests still pending.
Last sampled error line of the 'timeout exceeded when trying to connect' pattern.

hypotheses.statement: Saturation of the connection pool at its {pool_max}-connection cap caused the incident: requests queueing for connections (pool_pending at {pend_max}, pool_wait_p95 at {wait_max} s) made HTTP p95 latency reach {lat_max} s and drove the 5xx ratio to {err_max} via 'timeout exceeded when trying to connect' errors.

A slow or leaked connection holder kept connections checked out of the pool until all {used_max} slots were occupied, which caused the pool to saturate and requests to time out while waiting for a connection.
Elevated database operation latency caused the request latency and 5xx spike.
Event-loop / CPU saturation inside demo-service caused the latency and error spike.
A surge in inbound request rate overloaded the service and caused the latency and 5xx spike.

observations.statement: HTTP p95 latency was flat at {lat_first} s at 14:28:26 and stayed at the same millisecond level through 14:30:11, then jumped to {lat_mid} s at 14:30:26 and reached {lat_max} s at 14:30:41.
5xx error ratio was {err_base} at 14:28:26 and stayed there through 14:30:11, then rose to {err_mid} at 14:30:26 and peaked at {err_max} at 14:30:41.
Pool used connections were {used_base} at 14:28:26 and climbed from {used_prev} at 14:29:11 to {used_max} connections at 14:30:26, i.e. the pool was fully utilized at its cap.
The pool hard cap was constant at {pool_max} connections over the whole window.
Pool pending (queued) requests sat at {pend_base} in the baseline window ending 14:28:26 and then jumped to {pend_max} queued requests at 14:30:26, staying there at 14:30:41.

Pool wait p95 was {wait_base} s at 14:28:26 and stayed at millisecond level through 14:30:11, then rose to {wait_max} s at 14:30:41, which matches the HTTP p95 latency {lat_at_max} s in the same scrape.

Loki error log pattern sampling returned a single dominant pattern, 'request failed' with exception message 'timeout exceeded when trying to connect', {pat_count} sampled lines from 14:30:25.696Z to 14:30:42.608Z on service version 1.0.1.
Log volume shows an error-class burst summing to {log_err_sum} error lines in a single bucket, against {log_warn_sum} warn lines over four buckets.
Database operation p95 stayed flat and tiny, between {db_min} s and {db_max} s, across the entire window including the incident onset.
Event-loop delay p99 stayed between {el_min} s and {el_max} s with no trend change at the incident onset.
Request rate stayed essentially flat between {rps_min} req/s and {rps_max} req/s across the window, showing no traffic surge at the onset.

recommendations.action: Raise the database connection-pool size above its current cap (or add read replicas / a pooler) so that large pending queues are absorbed instead of timing out.
recommendations.rationale: The pool was fully used at its cap with many pending requests and multi-second p95 wait, which matches the HTTP latency and 5xx spike.

recommendations.action: Add alerting on pool_pending and pool_wait_p95 so saturation is detected before the HTTP SLOs breach.
recommendations.rationale: Pool queueing and wait p95 spiked at the same scrape as the latency and error jump; these signals are more specific than service latency.

recommendations.action: Instrument and cap connection checkout time with a bounded acquire timeout, and log which code path holds connections, to find long-held or leaked connections.
recommendations.rationale: Pool occupancy began rising about a minute before full saturation, so a slow or leaked holder cannot be excluded and must be identified.

recommendations.action: Verify database-side metrics (connection count, slow queries, lock waits) during future occurrences even though operation p95 stayed flat, to confirm no work is being done while connections are held.
recommendations.rationale: DB operation p95 stayed flat at a few milliseconds, contradicting slow queries as the driver, but client-side holding time was not measured.
